newsitem.title: UK: British Aerospace wins $700 million Hawk order.
newsitem.headline: British Aerospace wins $700 million Hawk order.

text.p: British Aerospace said on Sunday it had won an order worth 425 million pounds ($700.5 million) for more than 30 Hawk aircraft for Australia.
"The deal is worth 425 million pounds," a BAE spokeswoman told Reuters.
Australian Prime Minister John Howard announced the deal after holding talks with BAE chief Richard Evans and Defence Secretary George Robertson during a visit to Warton factory in northern England.

"The British government is indeed proud, and extremely pleased, that the Commonwealth of Australia has selected the Hawk to meet the Royal Australian Air Force's lead-in fighter requirement," British Defence Minister George Robertson said in a statement.
"The project is a shining example of British and Australian industry forging new and mutually beneficial partnerships."
Robertson added that other British firms were interested in development partnerships with Australian industry and the government was keen to encourage closer co-operation.

British Aerospace was selected as the preferred candidate for the order last November. The company will invest in a new plant in northern England to assemble 12 aircraft in Britain and another 21 planes will be built in Australia.
The spokeswoman said the deal will be signed next week "probably on Tuesday" in Canberra.
